question: What is the resource-pressure relationship between finite dormant associative storage and preservation of previously learned cue-response capability under stable and abruptly changed tasks?
hypothesis: Under stable targets more dormant memory generally helps returning-motif accuracy; under a target switch it may retain stale responses and harm adaptation. The capacity gradient should be reported without selecting an advantageous budget after results.
generator: Exactly original Y033 SHA256-keyed motif schedule on 16 motif identities, 7 active each episode and 12 episodes per seed. Targets SHA256('Y033/'+seed+'/'+motif) first byte modulo4; STABLE unchanged and SWITCH globally adds2 modulo4 from episode6. Only the seven current observed labels become available after policy predicts them.
policy: For cap k, retain seven previous-active observed cue/value pairs as live and at most k inactive observed cue/value pairs in an ordered oldest-evicted cache. Predict from live, then dormant, else fallback class0. Update stored cue values only after observing feedback. Both capacity reduction and cache writes/evictions must be charged explicitly; never exceed 7+k <=16 storage.
primary: For heldout seeds across caps k∈{0,3,6,9}, report stable total correct out of 4x12x7=336, stable returning-dormant correct, switch pre/post-change correct, post-switch stale-memory errors, total cache insertions, evictions and occupancy. CAPACITY_RECALL_GRADIENT if stable accuracy is nondecreasing with k and k9>k0; NONMONOTONE otherwise. No preferred k selection based on observed values.
validation: All eight seed/target SHA256 signatures unique, exact 7 live /<=k dormant assertions, no oracle/future labels available to policy, deterministic run() twice, first-use original result, one full pytest regression and original Git prereg/source SHA pins.
claim_limit: Finite synthetic associative memory capacity-vs-adaptation tradeoff; not evidence of biological intelligence, real-world semantic memory or adaptive substrate growth.
